title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 75-77): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'polynomial structure' on a category P with finite products. The hom-groups P(X,Y) are thought of as polynomial maps. The degree-1 parts form an additive category P_1, and the goal (next page) is to recover tensor products X⊗Y and divided powers Γ^n X by representability. This presumably serves to handle multiplicative structures (products, divided powers) on complexes in the dévissage of the title.

Axiom (d), previous page: P(X_1×...×X_r, Y) = ⊕_{n∈N^r} P_n(X_1,...,X_r;Y). Here f∈P_n means f∘(λ_1 id,...,λ_r id) = λ^n f for λ∈Z^r.

Top of this page (crossed out): he finishes his attempted uniqueness proof. Take g∈P_{n'} that is also an eigenvector for the character λ^n. Then (λ^n − λ^{n'})g = 0 for all λ∈Z^r, and it would suffice that the integers λ^n − λ^{n'} generate the unit ideal. They do not: for example λ−λ^3 is always divisible by 6, and λ^p ≡ λ mod p. So uniqueness fails in the presence of torsion. He abandons the argument.

He then considers two remedies.
- Base change: require, for every Z-algebra h, compositions on P_h(X,Y)=P(X,Y)⊗h, and the decomposition to hold in P_h(ΠX_i,Y) for λ∈(h^×)^r. This is the familiar trick that rigidifies polynomial maps into 'strict' ones, as in Roby's polynomial laws.
- Extra structure: make the decomposition (*) part of the data. This is the option he adopts.

He then lists compatibility axioms.
- (e) Degree condition: if f: X_1×...×X_r→Y has multidegree (n_1..n_r) and g_i: Z^i_1×...×Z^i_{s_i}→X_i has multidegree (m^i_1..m^i_{s_i}), then f∘(g_1,...,g_r) has degree n_i m^i_j in Z^i_j. A margin note treats the case n_i=0.
- (f) Compatibility with permutation of factors.
- (g) Constants: for X→0 (0 the terminal object), P_0(0,Y)→P_0(X,Y) is bijective, i.e. degree-0 maps are constants independent of X.

Definition: if h is a commutative ring acting h-linearly via h→End(id_{P_1})→End(P), and homogeneity holds for all λ∈h^r, P is called 'h-polynomial'.

Next page: ⊗ represents bilinear maps P_{(1,1)}(X,Y;−), and Γ^n X represents P_n(X,−) on P_1. This matches Roby's Γ^n as the universal recipient of homogeneous degree-n polynomial laws, i.e. the framework later formalized as strict polynomial functors (Friedlander–Suslin) and the categories Γ^d P.
errors: The (crossed-out) uniqueness argument fails: the values λ^n − λ^{n'} for λ∈Z^r need not generate the unit ideal of Z (e.g. λ−λ^3 ≡ 0 mod 6; Frobenius-type coincidences mod p). Uniqueness of the grading fails with torsion. Grothendieck evidently noticed this, crossed it out, and switched to base change or extra structure.
'λ∈Z^n' / 'λ∈(h^×)^n' should read Z^r, (h^×)^r (index set of factors) - notational slip.
Axiom (e) as stated only makes sense for homogeneous g_i; for general g_i one must expand into homogeneous components. Implicit but fine.

Under the base-change remedy, the invertibility requirement λ∈(h^×)^r is somewhat odd: homogeneity for all λ∈h^r is what is needed, as in the later h-polynomial definition. Over finite h, units alone may not separate degrees.

ideas.what: Uniqueness of a multigrading defined by eigenvalues of scalar multiplication fails over Z because of torsion; remedy by base change to all Z-algebras or by making the grading part of the structure
ideas.modern_name: Strict vs. non-strict polynomial maps; polynomial laws (Roby); grading from G_m-action
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963) for polynomial laws; Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors
ideas.where_published: Gradings via G_m-actions appear in SGA 3 style; not this specific discussion

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'polynomial category': category with finite products whose hom-groups out of products carry a multigrading by degree, compatible with composition (degrees multiply), symmetry, and constants
ideas.modern_name: Categories of polynomial maps; close to Lawvere theories of commutative algebras; enrichment underlying strict polynomial functors (Γ^d P)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single standard source; related to Friedlander–Suslin, Krause, Touzé on strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Degree multiplicativity under composition (axiom e) and constants axiom (g)
h-polynomial structure: h acting through the center of the additive part P_1, with homogeneity for all λ∈h^r

missed.claim: An axiomatic definition of a 'polynomial category' P (degree-graded homs out of products, degree-multiplicative composition, symmetry, constants), from whose degree-1 part ⊗ and Γ^n are to be recovered by representability. This anticipates the representing objects Γ^n of strict polynomial functors. The axiomatics were not developed further here and do not seem to appear in Grothendieck's circulated texts.
missed.quote: On va mettre comme structure supplémentaire la donnée de la décomposition (*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An intrinsic characterization of 'categories of polynomial maps' (rather than Γ^d P built from a given additive P) is not standard. It could give an alternative foundation for strict polynomial functors and divided-power structures on complexes. Given the routine nature of the individual axioms, this is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: Coherent, early (c. 1975-76) axiomatization of polynomial-map categories with Γ^n defined by representability. It is conceptually close to the later strict polynomial functor theory (Friedlander–Suslin 1997), but each step is fairly routine and Roby's Γ^n and polynomial laws predate it. Mildly notable as an unpublished precursor.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'g_{n,n'}' is likely 'g_{n'}' (continuing the previous page), and 'Z^n' likely stands for Z^r.
'si P, est muni' should read 'si P_1 est muni' (the h-linear structure on P_1).
'telle que ce plus haut soit vrai' is likely 'telle que (d) plus haut soit vrai'.
Line 3, '[?] en exigeant...': possibly 'On s'en tire en exigeant...' or similar; the crossed-out start reads roughly 'l'idéal 1, ou [bien]...'.
Margin note top right is roughly 'Oubli: on a exigé que les P_i ... sous-groupes ... de P(X,Y) et P(X,Y) = ⊕ P_i(X,Y)' (the decomposition is a direct-sum decomposition of the hom-group).
